sections.shortlist: Active core projects at a glance

templates.current:
**{total} projects, of which {baseline} come from the three original research reports and {added} were added in this round.** Feature verification: {reviewed}; metrics snapshot: `{as_of}` (UTC).

Within each category, projects are first tiered by maintenance status, then ranked by a blend of stars (40%), 90-day default-branch commits (35%) and recency of the last commit (25%). Archived projects are placed last. The maintenance score describes GitHub popularity and activity signals only; it does not represent memory accuracy, cost, safety or production maturity.
templates.shortlist_note: Shows only core candidates with a verified license and commits in the last 90 days; research implementations, retrieval components, restricted-license and historical projects are excluded from this table.
templates.toc_note: `★Report baseline` marks projects coming from the three user-provided research reports. Each entry has exactly one primary category, so the same repository never enters the ranking twice.
templates.detail_intro: Feature judgments come from the official README at a pinned commit; not every project was installed and run. Daily metrics refreshes do not automatically re-audit features or licenses.
templates.rankings_intro: Snapshot: `{as_of}`. This is a ranking of GitHub maintenance metadata, not a memory-capability leaderboard. All views tier by maintenance status first; raw values are in the [CSV]({R}data/rankings.csv).
templates.choose:
- Need a complete external memory API: start with memory engines and services.
- Need memory you can review, edit and manage with Git directly: see file-backed source-of-truth memory.
- Need entity relations, temporal validity and multi-hop queries: see graph and temporal memory.
- Need memory across hosts such as Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode: see coding agents/MCP.
- Need to turn successes and failures into executable methods: see experience, skills and procedural memory.
- Need to verify effectiveness, poisoning, deletion and forgetting: see research implementations and benchmarks.

Full boundaries in [project details](docs/projects.md); category definitions in [Scope and taxonomy](docs/taxonomy.md).

```sh
python scripts/refresh_metrics.py
python scripts/build.py
python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
python scripts/build.py --check
```

GitHub Actions refreshes the GitHub metrics daily. Adding projects and verifying features, categories and license judgments requires manual review.
templates.thanks:
Original curation and scripts in this catalogue use the [MIT]({R}LICENSE); linked projects follow their own licenses. Unknown, compound, non-commercial and BSL/PolyForm projects keep their original boundaries.

The initial classification and project map come from three user-provided local research reports; this round also referenced [mnemoverse/awesome-agent-memory](https://github.com/mnemoverse/awesome-agent-memory) for coverage checks, with every entry verified against its official repository.
templates.records_note: The [change records]({R}record/) keep the original text (Chinese) as written at verification time, so the source and wording of every judgment stay auditable.
